checks.intent: Identify the exact host, device, mountpoint, filesystem type, capacity, available bytes, and trend that triggered the alert
checks.confirms_when: A series identifies one alerting host, device, and mountpoint with less than the configured free-space threshold
checks.falsifies_when: No matching filesystem series breached the alert threshold during the incident window

checks.intent: Read the configured infrastructure repository to identify the approved host route and candidate service storage paths

invocation.template: Read the configured infrastructure repository metadata, monitoring stack README, host inventory policy, Compose topology, and production inventory. Return the approved host identity and candidate service storage paths without reading credentials.

checks.confirms_when: Reviewed documentation identifies an approved host route and candidate storage paths for the alerted service
checks.falsifies_when: Reviewed documentation explicitly shows the suspected service does not run on the alerting host

checks.intent: Map the alerted filesystem and every suspected service storage path to runtime host, device, and mountpoint identities

invocation.template: Use the reviewed bounded host evidence wrapper to map root, monitoring, and container storage paths to host, device, mountpoint, and filesystem identities. Compare candidates only with explicit resource identity keys.

checks.confirms_when: The suspected consumer maps to the same host, device, and mountpoint as the alert, with the join keys recorded
checks.falsifies_when: The suspected consumer explicitly maps to a different device or mountpoint on the alerting host

checks.intent: Identify bounded top-level consumers on the alerted filesystem without crossing mount boundaries

invocation.template: Use the reviewed bounded host evidence wrapper to list top-level consumers on the alerted filesystem only. Do not follow other mounts and do not read file contents, configuration, environment, or credentials.

checks.confirms_when: One or more bounded consumers on the alerted filesystem account for material usage and are identified by path and bytes
checks.falsifies_when: No inspected consumer on the alerted filesystem accounts for material usage within the bounded evidence

checks.intent: Verify current free-space headroom for the original alert host, device, and mountpoint
checks.confirms_when: The original host, device, and mountpoint have recovered above the responder-approved free-space threshold
checks.falsifies_when: The original filesystem remains below the threshold or the returned resource identity differs

escalation.when: Runtime topology is unavailable, resource identities do not match, or no bounded consumer explains the alert

proposed_steps: Ask the infrastructure owner to review evidence-linked consumers on the alerted filesystem and approve a reversible cleanup target.
Treat service storage or WAL failures on a different filesystem as a separate remediation task with its own owner and verification.
remediation.approval_expectation: The incident commander or infrastructure owner approves the exact target and rollback before any cleanup or service recovery action.
rollback_steps: Stop the approved cleanup if free space, service health, or evidence integrity worsens.
Restore only responder-approved reversible moves and re-run the original filesystem identity check.

notes: Never infer filesystem causality by dividing or comparing metrics with different host, device, or mountpoint identities. Unknown topology is an evidence gap, not a root cause.
